acceptanceCriteria: Freeze the CEM 1.0 wire/schema, canonical patch/hunk identities, immutable evidence and source-content-free boundary with explicit compatibility/migration for frozen 0.1/0.2/0.3 artifacts; all consumer surfaces agree on the new profile and unknown critical features refuse.

Bind canonical Tasks acceptance identity, ordered criteria, attempt generation, policy/configuration and exact candidate to provider-neutral test evidence; historical integrity remains valid after drift while live applicability refuses stale records.

Freeze and implement actual execution support for all main test runners of every supported language, including every existing registered affected-test runner. Discovery, result import, a parser and generic successful command must not substitute for runner execution qualification; no language or runner is silently deferred.

Retain exact test/parameter/suite/project identity, all attempts/retries and framework statuses; distinguish test assertions, build/collection/setup/infrastructure errors, skip/disabled/no-tests, timeout/interruption and missing/conflicting reports without false passes or killed controls.

Qualify fixed runner invocation, runtime/tool/dependency and application/device identities, bounded outputs, cancellation/descendant cleanup and immutable inputs on actual representative runners. Preserve unavailable tuples as release blockers, with required platform/device evidence rather than synthetic success.

Independent portable producer/consumer conformance, actual native Tasks lifecycle and cross-language CEM integration, compatibility fixtures, release-required checks and one independent review bind one final artifact set. Feasibility is not superiority; research outcome study remains separate and visible.

Corvint v1-0 release explicitly requires completed CEM 1.0 work; native completion and release readiness retain unfinished provider/platform, interoperability or promotion evidence. Owner promotion is explicit; old experimental numbers cannot be relabeled stable.
body: Owner scope amendment 2026-10-01: "I want to get CEM to v1.0 for the main v1.0 release"; "we are supposted to be supporting all the main test runners for all the languages we support"; "work on all these in parallell". Usage credits explicitly authorized. This is the release target and execution-coverage requirement, not a promotion receipt. Existing research V1-0573 and prototype V1-0575 remain open with their original evidence obligations. Current public source has eight affected-language adapters and sixteen candidate analyzer families; runner execution and test discovery must be audited separately. Main-runner inventory must include every existing registered runner plus primary frameworks for each supported language; candidate/domain ambiguity needs explicit retained disposition rather than silent omission. Parallel lanes dynamic, native and platform use one shared experimental runner contract and one Tasks boundary lane; no default queue cutover or wire relabeling. Release promotion and merge authority remain separate.
title: CEM 1.0: stable task-linked evidence with all main supported test runners
